engine.meaning: The original almost word for word, so every point survives: "No single operator is acceptable as the custodian of the inputs."
engine.sense: The few changes fit: "knock together an auction", "adds 'em", "wanna know".
engine.authenticity: Barely any Aussie, and one form is not Australian at all: "decryption each 'ave a deadline" is a Cockney h-drop. The rest is ya and yer dropped into the doc: "ya can compare yer task".
engine.register: Largely untranslated, far from level 5: "The result is a computation that BFV supports well, for example a sum, a count, or a tally."
engine.flow: Reads as the original does, with a jolt at "each 'ave a".
engine.variety: Almost no slang to vary: ya, yer, 'em, "knock together".
engine.essence: Recognisably the doc because it nearly is the doc; nothing retold.

yarn-troppo.meaning: Every point, limit and table row is kept, and asides elaborate correctly: "a tally with one vote in it, say, and everyone knows how that one voted", "Bigger committee, bigger bill." One narrowing: "the only thing that ever gets decrypted is who won" for the auction result, which could include price.
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "tots up" for adds, "suss out" for know, "the bouncer" for the program deciding inputs, "stuff up the result", "chews through the limited noise budget".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Mostly sounds like an Aussie dev talking: "So when's an E3 the go?", "Nobody gets to be the bloke holdin' the keys to the shed." Some stock or imported lines: "Here's the poster child.", "The whole box and dice.", "this one's a ripper".
yarn-troppo.register: A full level-5 telling with asides throughout: "An E3's no drive-through: there's no real-time result.", "Righto, before ya go designin' an E3 program, run yer eye over these." No swearing, within the brief.
yarn-troppo.tone: Keeps the cautionary weight of the limits ("Every one of 'em can bite", "But don't kid yerself"), though the opener "Now, this one's a ripper" talks up the page in a way the plain doc doesn't.
yarn-troppo.flow: Lively, but asides stack up in places: "It's a full E3 program for secret ballots, start to finish, and it actually works. Here's", "The template and CRISP only ever use homomorphic addition, and that's it."
yarn-troppo.variety: Varied throughout: "suss out", "ticks these boxes", "tots up", "the bouncer", "chews through", "leg up", "under wraps".
yarn-troppo.essence: Unmistakably the Interfold use-cases page, retold, with its table, limits and link cards intact.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every point and limit kept, cleanly: "Without an input proof, a malformed ciphertext can stuff up the result or bring the E3 to a halt."
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "the go", "chip in inputs", "holdin' the lot", "hang about", "Run yer eye over", "a leg up".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural throughout, nothing stock: "Ya can't have any one operator holdin' the lot.", "Best place to start is the".
yarn-dinkum.register: Colloquial and talked through, but a measured retelling rather than a level-5 yarn; the table and limits stay close to the doc: "The plaintext output goes on-chain."
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the clear, cautionary doc tone whole.
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "The application can hang about while the E3 goes through its stages. Don't expect a real-time result out of an E3."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied without leaning: "ticks these boxes", "right up the E3 model's alley", "eats into", "stuff up".

yarn-deadset.meaning: Every point kept: "Workin' that out is on the application owner."
yarn-deadset.sense: Terms fit: "chip in", "hits the wall", "stuff up", "Kick off with".
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural word swaps, but some lines keep the doc's stiff syntax: "No single operator is okay as the one holdin' the inputs."
yarn-deadset.register: Light, mostly the doc with words swapped: "A design can also decrypt an aggregate, for example the number of bids at each price level.", well short of level 5.
yarn-deadset.flow: Mostly smooth, with one stiff join: "No single operator is okay as the one holdin' the inputs."
yarn-deadset.variety: A few terms carry it: "ticks these boxes", "chip in", "hang about", "work out" three times.
yarn-deadset.essence: Clearly the use-cases page, lightly retold.

unharnessed.meaning: Every point kept; additions hang off the original ("for all the world to see", "so don't get your hopes up"), though the last link card is rewritten: "Design rules for E3 programs that won't leave you up the creek without a paddle."
unharnessed.sense: Mostly exact: "no skin off anyone's nose", "Each mob encrypts", "the committee's graft", "comes unstuck". "a dodgy ciphertext" for malformed suggests malice, and "tick every box for a regulation" softens compliant.
unharnessed.authenticity: Sounds Australian throughout: "Have a good squiz at these limits", "Kick off with". A few stock bolt-ons: "the whole box and dice", "up the creek without a paddle", "grinding halt".
unharnessed.register: Colloquial and retold throughout, "Righto, this page runs through the jobs that suit an E3", a shade under a full level-5 yarn. No swearing, within the brief.
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the cautions serious; one line edges flippant: "so don't get your hopes up".
unharnessed.flow: Smooth: "Bidders put in encrypted bids, and only the result of the auction gets decrypted."
unharnessed.variety: Varied, nothing leaned on: "no skin off anyone's nose", "whips up", "legit", "comes unstuck", "chews through", "mob", "graft", "squiz".
